disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Hawaii has no furbearer trapping program: there are no furbearer seasons, zones, or limits to model. Always verify current regulations with the Hawaii DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife before any trapping activity.

license_summary.indigenous_wildlife: Take (including trapping) of indigenous wildlife is prohibited under HAR Chapter 13-124.
license_summary.no_furbearer_program: Hawaii DLNR's hunting program covers game birds (HAR Chapter 13-122) and game mammals (HAR Chapter 13-123) — feral pigs, goats, deer, and sheep. There is no furbearer season structure, no furbearer trapping license, and no furbearing-animal harvest regulations.

sources.notes: DLNR hunting program homepage lists only Game Birds (HAR 13-122) and Game Mammals (HAR 13-123); no furbearer program exists.
sources.title: Hawaii DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife — Hunting (official page)

species.scientific_name_note: Informational record — Hawaii DLNR has no furbearer category; this is not a species.
species.iac_reference: Hawaii Administrative Rules Title 13 (no furbearer provisions; hunting rules cover game birds HAR 13-122 and game mammals HAR 13-123 only)
species.notes: Hawaii has no native furbearers and DLNR regulates no furbearer trapping seasons, licenses, or bag limits. Feral game mammals (pig, goat, deer, sheep) are hunted under game-mammal rules, not furbearer seasons, and are intentionally excluded. The app flags any furbearer-species log in Hawaii as out of season.

verification.confirmation_notes: Verified 2026-09-18 from the DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife hunting page: Hawaii's regulated hunting covers game birds and game mammals (feral pig, goat, deer, sheep). No furbearer trapping seasons, licenses, or regulations exist in the current DLNR rules.
known_gaps: Feral pigs, goats, deer, and sheep are hunted in Hawaii but are NOT furbearers and are intentionally excluded — they must not be modeled as furbearer trapping seasons.
Any unlisted species (e.g., mongoose, feral cats/dogs) taken for damage control is not a regulated furbearer season and is not modeled here.
